title: Courier or Relay? Testing What Travels

scenes.visual: Dark background. Faint silhouette of the same sympathetic neuron and colour map from the first film (slate-white membrane, indigo nucleus left, gold NGF right, steel-blue microtubules). Title 'Courier or Relay? Testing What Travels' fades in cleanly at top center (size 36) and fades out before s01.

scenes.tts: The first film showed how a dynein-carried signaling endosome crosses a centimeter in hours. Since a relay could beat diffusion too, how can an experiment tell whether the receptor actually travels? Or does it stay at the tip while local signals march home?
scenes.caption: The first film showed how a dynein-carried signaling endosome crosses a centimeter in hours. Since a relay could beat diffusion too, how can an experiment tell whether the receptor actually travels? Or does it stay at the tip while local signals march home?
scenes.visual: Carry the same sympathetic neuron from the first film (labelled 'schematic'). An emerald dynein motor carrying a gold-teal-magenta signaling endosome glides leftward along the steel-blue microtubule. Halfway across, the axon smoothly splits vertically into two identical parallel axon tracks spanning left to right, with a clean question mark between them.
scenes.narration: The first film showed how a dynein-carried signaling endosome crosses a centimeter in hours. Since a relay could beat diffusion too, how can an experiment tell whether the receptor actually travels? Or does it stay at the tip while local signals march home?

scenes.tts: Picture two competing models on the same axon. In the courier model, one active NGF and track A endosome rides dynein all the way home. In the relay model, track A stays at the tip. Like a bucket brigade, each stretch hands a local signal to the next. Both wake nuclear Creb.
scenes.caption: Picture two competing models on the same axon. In the courier model, one active NGF and TrkA endosome rides dynein all the way home. In the relay model, TrkA stays at the tip. Like a bucket brigade, each stretch hands a local signal to the next. Both wake nuclear CREB.
scenes.visual: Two parallel horizontal axon tracks ('Courier' on top, 'Relay' on bottom), both ending at indigo nuclei on the left and receiving gold NGF on the right. Top track: one gold-teal-magenta endosome rides emerald dynein all the way from right tip to left nucleus. Bottom track: gold NGF and teal TrkA stay fixed at the right tip while sequential magenta pulses hop from segment to segment leftward like a bucket brigade. Both indigo nuclei light up 'CREB active'.
scenes.narration: Picture two competing models on the same axon. In the courier model, one active NGF and TrkA endosome rides dynein all the way home. In the relay model, TrkA stays at the tip. Like a bucket brigade, each stretch hands a local signal to the next. Both wake nuclear CREB.

scenes.tts: Timing alone cannot choose, because a fast relay can also arrive within hours. A natural next test is to disable the motor dynein. Suppose you give NGF only to the far axons, block dynein, and the neurons die. Predict: does death after blocking dynein prove one vesicle carried the receptor?
scenes.caption: Timing alone cannot choose, because a fast relay can also arrive within hours. A natural next test is to disable the motor dynein. Suppose you give NGF only to the far axons, block dynein, and the neurons die. Predict: does death after blocking dynein prove one vesicle carried the receptor?
scenes.visual: Keep the two parallel tracks visible. On a clean schematic test setup, a crimson red X locks over the emerald dynein motors. On the left, the cell body dims as a red outcome tag reads 'Neurons die'. Freeze the two tracks before revealing which ones stop, and display a crisp question card at bottom: 'Does blocking dynein prove a courier?'
scenes.narration: Timing alone cannot choose, because a fast relay can also arrive within hours. A natural next test is to disable the motor dynein. Suppose you give NGF only to the far axons, block dynein, and the neurons die. Predict: does death after blocking dynein prove one vesicle carried the receptor?

scenes.visual: Hold the split courier-and-relay tracks with the crimson X over dynein gently pulsing and the question card 'Does blocking dynein prove a courier?' clearly visible at full contrast. A subtle 4.5-second progress bar glides smoothly along the bottom edge.

scenes.tts: No, because both models can need dynein. Blocking it stops a courier endosome from leaving the tip. But a relay could also use dynein for short local handoffs within each stretch of axon. If each local step needs dynein, blocking the motor halts the brigade too. Both models predict death.
scenes.caption: No, because both models can need dynein. Blocking it stops a courier endosome from leaving the tip. But a relay could also use dynein for short local handoffs within each stretch of axon. If each local step needs dynein, blocking the motor halts the brigade too. Both models predict death.
scenes.visual: The question card clears. Top track (Courier): emerald dynein freezes under the crimson X, halting the endosome near the tip; its left nucleus dims ('Dies'). Bottom track (Relay, labelled 'if each local step needs dynein'): tiny emerald dynein motors shown assisting each local handoff also freeze under crimson X marks, stopping the bucket brigade dead; its left nucleus also dims ('Dies'). A clean comparison badge reads 'Same prediction — inconclusive'.
scenes.narration: No, because both models can need dynein. Blocking it stops a courier endosome from leaving the tip. But a relay could also use dynein for short local handoffs within each stretch of axon. If each local step needs dynein, blocking the motor halts the brigade too. Both models predict death.

scenes.tts: To tell two models apart, test an outcome only one predicts. Instead of stopping dynein everywhere, divide the axon across three sealed chambers: tip, middle stretch, and cell body. Now add a drug that blocks track A kinase activity only inside the middle chamber.
scenes.caption: To tell two models apart, test an outcome only one predicts. Instead of stopping dynein everywhere, divide the axon across three sealed chambers: tip, middle stretch, and cell body. Now add a drug that blocks TrkA kinase activity only inside the middle chamber.
scenes.visual: Clear the crimson X marks from dynein. Two vertical white-grey schematic barriers drop across both parallel axon tracks, creating three sealed compartments: 'Cell body' (left), 'Middle axon' (center), and 'Axon tip' (right, bathed in gold NGF). A crimson wash fills ONLY the center 'Middle axon' compartment, labelled 'TrkA inhibitor'.
scenes.narration: To tell two models apart, test an outcome only one predicts. Instead of stopping dynein everywhere, divide the axon across three sealed chambers: tip, middle stretch, and cell body. Now add a drug that blocks TrkA kinase activity only inside the middle chamber.

scenes.tts: Watch how the two tracks split. A relay passing track A activity from stretch to stretch hits the inhibitor and dies in the middle. The courier behaves differently. Even if the drug quiets its kinase during transit, dynein carries the vesicle through with NGF still bound inside. In the drug-free cell body, track A can signal again.
scenes.caption: Watch how the two tracks split. A relay passing TrkA activity from stretch to stretch hits the inhibitor and dies in the middle. The courier behaves differently. Even if the drug quiets its kinase during transit, dynein carries the vesicle through with NGF still bound inside. In the drug-free cell body, TrkA can signal again.
scenes.visual: Animate both tracks simultaneously. Bottom track (Relay): magenta kinase pulses hop leftward, hit the crimson middle chamber, and vanish completely; the left nucleus stays dark ('Predicts: fails'). Top track (Courier): emerald dynein carries the gold-and-teal vesicle straight through the crimson middle chamber—its magenta glow dims inside the drug zone while gold NGF stays visibly locked inside—then as it exits into the clear left chamber, the magenta kinase relights and illuminates the indigo nucleus ('Predicts: survives').
scenes.narration: Watch how the two tracks split. A relay passing TrkA activity from stretch to stretch hits the inhibitor and dies in the middle. The courier behaves differently. Even if the drug quiets its kinase during transit, dynein carries the vesicle through with NGF still bound inside. In the drug-free cell body, TrkA can signal again.

scenes.tts: In 2003 Ye and colleagues ran this test, and survival was spared. That argues against a propagating wave of track A activity. Still, what if another signal reached the cell body while NGF stayed behind? Neutralizing NGF once it arrives in the cell body takes survival away. So the carried ligand matters, though other routes remain open.
scenes.caption: In 2003 Ye and colleagues ran this test, and survival was spared. That argues against a propagating wave of TrkA activity. Still, what if another signal reached the cell body while NGF stayed behind? Neutralizing NGF once it arrives in the cell body takes survival away. So the carried ligand matters, though other routes remain open.
scenes.visual: First, on the courier track, a small result tag appears as spoken: 'Observed: cell-body TrkA signaling and survival spared (Ye et al., 2003)'. Then the crimson wash clears from the middle chamber. Inside the left 'Cell body' chamber, crimson Y-shaped neutralizing antibodies bind the arriving gold NGF, extinguishing the magenta kinase glow and dimming the indigo nucleus ('Survival fails'). A subtle honest label reads 'Supports carried NGF-TrkA; other routes open'.
scenes.narration: In 2003 Ye and colleagues ran this test, and survival was spared. That argues against a propagating wave of TrkA activity. Still, what if another signal reached the cell body while NGF stayed behind? Neutralizing NGF once it arrives in the cell body takes survival away. So the carried ligand matters, though other routes remain open.

scenes.tts: Notice why the three-chamber design succeeded where disabling dynein failed. A perturbation that breaks a shared requirement can never separate rival mechanisms. When two hypotheses both fit the timing, aim your test at the exact step where their predictions diverge.
scenes.caption: Notice why the three-chamber design succeeded where disabling dynein failed. A perturbation that breaks a shared requirement can never separate rival mechanisms. When two hypotheses both fit the timing, aim your test at the exact step where their predictions diverge.
scenes.visual: Compact visual recap over the two parallel tracks: a split miniature showing 'Dynein block → both fail' dimming on the left, while 'Middle TrkA block → courier survives, relay fails' highlights cleanly on the right, preserving the exact colour map.
scenes.narration: Notice why the three-chamber design succeeded where disabling dynein failed. A perturbation that breaks a shared requirement can never separate rival mechanisms. When two hypotheses both fit the timing, aim your test at the exact step where their predictions diverge.

scenes.visual: Clean dark end card displaying one line only, centered in large crisp white text (size 38), with no subtitle or smaller line underneath: 'To separate courier from relay, test what only one model predicts.'
